sourceEvidence.title: General Manager - Automotive Manufacturing
sourceEvidence.quote:
GENERAL SUMMARY
 
Plans, advises, consults, leads, and coordinates manufacturing, manufacturing support, and administration and organizational development activities for one or multiple facilities through Production, Engineering, Maintenance, Purchasing, Quality, Tooling, and Production Control to ensure efficient production of parts with the best material usage, quality levels, and service that exceed the customer’s expectations. Responsible for ensuring all key measures are met from plant and business operations. Leads and promotes matters related to safety, health, environmental, labor control, equipment, material, processes, and customer relations.
 
ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS
 
A. Serve as management consultant to assigned locations ensuring the management of the company aligns with North American Stamping Group, LLC standard operating procedures and provide subject matter expertise and assistance to increase operating and management efficiency.
 
B. Lead, plan, and manage all manufacturing activities and related functions at assigned locations including production, engineering, maintenance, purchasing, quality, tooling, and production control to ensure safety and quality and to meet and exceed customer and company requirements.
 
1. Lead manufacturing supervision in utilizing Total Quality Production System (TQPS) techniques to standardize processes/methods and to identify manufacturing problems and raw materials/components supply, and eliminate waste.
 
2. Ensure that feasibility studies are carried out correctly for the products to be manufactured at the facility, compatible with the footprint, investment, and quality capabilities planned.
 
3. Develop and monitor Lean activities and a manufacturing continuous improvement system.
 
4. Review launch products and engineering changes implementation and provide direction for successful launch.
 
5. Plan and organize layouts for line changes due to volume changes or manpower reductions.
 
6. Maintain contact with interdepartmental managers to provide feedback when dealing with process or material changes.
 
7. Hold daily staff meetings to communicate daily objectives and discuss successes, failures, and countermeasure activity.
 
8. Ensure NASG philosophies, systems, and processes are being followed at all times.
 
9. Maintain Master Capacity Plan for the facility for accurate budget and capital needs.
